answer: The tailor chalks his mark on every coat he cuts and enters the cloth in his ledger against the gentleman who ordered it. A oasis coat bought off the peg fails the ledger: at the forge of the chalk the cut must match the tailor's own shears, and a peg coat fits no man properly. Forging a coat means hiring a tailor, buying false cloth and paying 10,100, and the zephyr entry in the chalk ledger is read at every fitting, so a coat whose mark was never entered is unpicked.
